name: Steamed black chicken
summary: Steamed black chicken from Tủa Chùa, a Hmong bird on the culture desk. Vietnam News gives the local name ka đu and a half-hour steam over charcoal. The same article names a roast with hạt dổi, a hotpot, and a porridge, without those methods. A price is Check on arrival.
origin: Tua Chua, in Dien Bien. The culture desk keeps the bird in Tủa Chùa. It is not a basin-market breakfast. Vietnam News quotes a resident there.
culture: The culture desk says the bird sleeps in trees, drinks dew, and eats horse-tooth maize and tail rice, and that its glutamic and its iron are twice an ordinary chicken. Vietnam News says the skin and bones are black, the feathers black, white, grey, or yellow, and that it sleeps in trees and eats local maize and rice. Giàng A Páo, quoted there, calls it a precious medicine. That is his claim. A shop in the monument ward was not named.
taste: The culture desk says the meat is sweet, fragrant, and firm, and that steaming keeps the seasoning. Vietnam News says savoury, fragrant, and firm, after local spices and herbs.
howToEat: The culture desk describes it steamed, so the sweet meat and the seasoning stay. It does not print a time.
Vietnam News: soak the bird with local spices and herbs for 20 minutes, tie it with lemongrass leaves, and steam it over charcoal for half an hour.
The same resident names roasted chicken with hạt dổi, chicken in a hotpot, and porridge. Those methods were not printed. Check on arrival.
